# univaBio Backend

FastAPI + SQLite backend for the doctor–patient follow-up assistant.

A consultation **session** stores the conversation **transcript** and an embedded
**clinical report** generated by a free LLM API (**Groq**, OpenAI-compatible and
pluggable). Speech-to-text is out of scope for now — the API accepts transcript text.

## Roles
- **super_admin** — credentials from env (`SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME`, `SUPER_ADMIN_PASS`); creates doctor profiles.
- **doctor** — logs in with `username` + password; owns many patients.
- **patient** — identified/logs in by `phone`; belongs to exactly one doctor.

## Data model (3 tables)
- `doctor` 1 — * `patient` (patient has one doctor)
- `patient` 1 — * `session` (session belongs to one patient)
- `session` holds the transcript + clinical report fields (`summary`, `symptoms`,
  `issues_discussed`, `diagnosis`, `action_steps`, `medications`, `follow_up`, `report_raw`).

## Setup

```bash
cd Backend
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate          # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

cp .env.example .env              # then edit .env
```

In `.env`, set at minimum:
- `JWT_SECRET_KEY` — a long random string
- `SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME`, `SUPER_ADMIN_PASS`
- `GROQ_API_KEY` — free key from https://console.groq.com/keys
  (without it, sessions still save the transcript with `report_status = "pending_key"`)

## Run

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

- Interactive API docs: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
- Health check: http://127.0.0.1:8000/health

Optionally seed demo data (doctor `drsmith` / patient `+15550001111`):

```bash
python seed.py
```

## Key endpoints
| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/auth/login` | – | Login for super_admin / doctor / patient, returns JWT |
| POST | `/admin/doctors` | super_admin | Create a doctor profile |
| GET | `/admin/doctors` | super_admin | List doctors |
| GET | `/doctors/me` | doctor | Doctor profile |
| GET | `/doctors/me/patients` | doctor | Dashboard roster (session counts, last visit) |
| POST | `/patients` | doctor | Create a patient (by phone) |
| GET | `/patients/{phone}` | owner doctor / patient | Patient details |
| PATCH | `/patients/{phone}` | owner doctor / patient | Update patient |
| GET | `/patients/{phone}/history` | owner doctor / patient | All sessions + reports, newest first |
| POST | `/patients/{phone}/sessions` | owner doctor / patient | Add transcript → generates clinical report |
| GET | `/sessions/{id}` | owner doctor / patient | Session with report |
| POST | `/sessions/{id}/regenerate-report` | owner doctor / patient | Re-run the LLM on the stored transcript |

## Typical flow
1. Super admin logs in and creates a doctor.
2. Doctor logs in, creates patients (phone = identifier).
3. After a visit, doctor POSTs the transcript to `/patients/{phone}/sessions`;
   the backend returns the structured clinical report.
4. On follow-up, the doctor opens `/patients/{phone}/history` for the full timeline;
   the patient can log in with their phone to see the same history.

## Switching LLM provider
The provider is pluggable via `LLM_PROVIDER` + base URL/key. Any OpenAI-compatible
endpoint (Groq, OpenAI, Gemini-compatible gateways) works by pointing
`GROQ_BASE_URL`/`GROQ_MODEL`/`GROQ_API_KEY` (or adding a new provider class in
`app/llm/`).
